_doc: The intentional delta for the Own.NET startColumn producer slice.
WHAT THE SLICE DOES: the Roslyn extractor now stamps the 1-based column of a
subscription's event access onto the OwnIR fact, the core carries it on
Finding.column, and SARIF emits it as region.startColumn. Nothing about WHICH
findings exist changes - only where each one is anchored, and only in the
coordinate that was previously absent.
SO THE EXPECTATION IS NARROW ON PURPOSE. One producer (own-check), one field
(start_column), one transition (absent -> a real positive integer). A column
that MOVES from one integer to another is not this slice and is not signed off
here; neither is a line moving, a path moving, or a finding appearing or
disappearing.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED: occurrence coverage. A richer anchor can only
help it, but it may legitimately stay flat - a corpus run without a provenance
manifest earns no occurrence ids at all, and a line-only anchor that was
already unique in its run earns one either way. Pinning it unchanged would fail
honest runs; pinning it to increase would assert an improvement the slice does
not promise. It is reported, and `occurrence_coverage_decrease` is a change
kind, so a REGRESSION still surfaces without a pin.
Ambiguity is in `forbidden` rather than merely reported: the whole argument for
a column is that it discriminates. A slice that added columns AND left more
anchors indistinguishable than it found has disproved its own premise.

allowed_changes._doc: own-check reported a column for 0 of 613 results in the recorded STS corpus; every one of these is that absence being filled in.
